title: fix(agents): steers miss the next request during preparation
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a steer accepted while an embedded turn prepares its next request misses that request and waits through an unnecessary model response, including after a failed Code Mode cell.

## User Impact

Corrections accepted during continuation preparation or background-result placement enter the next model request. One-at-a-time steering, FIFO delivery, cancellation, and exact-once transcript commitment remain intact. This does not interrupt non-interruptible tools or shorten the existing settlement ceiling.

## Why This Change Was Made

The loop checked for input before awaited request preparation, leaving a gap before inference. Move the initial checkpoint after preparation and check that boundary on continuations that have not already consumed a queued batch. Consolidate the duplicated input-commit loops into the existing steering owner, retaining cancellation checks around message-start publication and input-scope commitment before message-end publication.

Delivery confirmation measures transcript settlement and can lag provider injection. This change targets the reproduced checkpoint gap before model dispatch.

## Evidence

Acceptance rule: synthetic input arriving during request preparation must appear in the immediately following model request exactly once. With a controlled 100 ms model-response hold, avoid the extra response, improve injection latency, and do not regress measured CPU/allocation. Run five serial interleaved baseline/candidate processes per timing/allocation mode; unchanged baseline repetitions are the A/A control. Report median/p95 and spread, host load, and filesystem separately. Startup and fixture generation are excluded.

The Code Mode regression was red on parent `53368c0ef6de7b224833b860b89d4e633cfe02eb`: corrections accepted during request preparation were absent from the immediately following provider request. Arrival during the failing tool already worked. Final focused loop/Code Mode/prefix tests pass 143/143; sessions_send admission and direct-announce fallback/cancellation pass 25/25. Browser components pass 6/6, bundled steering e2e 2/2, and the rebuilt isolated real-Gateway Send now flow 1/1 (scripted inference, real foreground execution). Codex autoreview is clean at P0–P2 after repairing a reviewed one-at-a-time continuation regression.

Five interleaved process pairs, 100 measured steers per revision; allocation measured separately in five further pairs:

| Warm owner metric | Parent | Fix |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Model requests per input | 2 | 1 |
| Injection median / p95 | 102.700 / 104.621 ms | 0.138 / 0.330 ms |
| Injection min–max | 100.796–120.661 ms | 0.105–0.968 ms |
| Main CPU per input, median | 1.990 ms | 1.012 ms |
| Process CPU per input, median | 3.531 ms | 2.144 ms |
| Sampled allocated bytes/input, median | 449,286 | 299,367 |

A/A baseline run medians span 101.747–103.080 ms. Baseline main CPU spans 1.684–2.204 ms/input, candidate 0.952–1.317; host load1 spans 33.1–62.8. CPU results remain host-sensitive. The response hold is intentionally synthetic: these are owner measurements, not live-provider latency. Separate baseline/candidate CPU profiles were captured.

Rerun: `node --expose-gc --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/inter-session-steering-measure.ts --scenario checkpoint --iterations 20 --hold-ms 100 --mode timing` (repeat with `--mode allocation`). The parent comparison uses the existing sparse baseline preload with the parent agent-loop.ts and identical remaining source/harness. `--state-dir` supports a generated team-shape fixture and `--workspace` its populated worktree.

Production delta is +15 lines. The additional checkpoint is necessary; consolidating the duplicated commitment path keeps cancellation and transcript publication under one implementation and shrinks the oversized loop file. No new cache, configuration, schema, or timeout.

Full `pnpm check:changed` passes. CI run [43374878911](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43374878911) completed successfully at `e53155f3e4312086187a0cb5e06af8910d1cc41d`. ClawSweeper reviewed that head with no findings or open checklist items. No inherited-failure exception is needed.

Two isolated live OpenAI `gpt-5.4` scenarios passed: same-requester input during preparation and compatible steering. These support eventual live delivery; the strict next-request-after-Code-Mode-failure invariant is proved by the embedded red/green regression, not asserted by those live scenarios. Linux capacity was unavailable; persisted scale proof uses APFS, not btrfs.

The synthetic fixture contains a 50,525,728,768-byte (47.06 GiB) agent database, 5,000 sessions, 265,549 transcript events, 6,000 settled runs, and 62,000 files totaling 1.116 GB. Transcript generation was stopped once actual database size exceeded the intended reference scale, then the existing fixture seeding owner completed run/workspace state and closed the database normally. No copied production data or sparse padding. The original logical transcript-byte target is not claimed.


Persisted owner results on that fixture (five interleaved process pairs per mode; 100 measured inputs per revision):

| Persisted owner metric | Parent | Fix |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Injection median / p95 | 111.105 / 144.448 ms | 3.552 / 5.978 ms |
| Injection min–max | 107.712–435.024 ms | 2.340–55.695 ms |
| Main CPU per input, median | 7.735 ms | 5.057 ms |
| Process CPU per input, median | 27.136 ms | 20.451 ms |
| Sampled allocated bytes/input, median | 1,753,108 | 1,256,478 |
| Requests per input | 2 | 1 |

Persisted A/A baseline run medians: 111.774, 110.903, 111.671, 111.130, 109.449 ms. Candidate run medians: 4.194, 3.988, 3.597, 3.148, 2.587 ms. Main CPU spans 6.096–18.252 ms/input on the baseline and 4.099–5.753 on the fix; host load1 spans 13.4–32.3. All exact-once assertions passed. Allocation samples span 1,735,636–1,762,109 bytes/input on the baseline and 1,253,861–1,260,449 on the fix. The busy host affects CPU and tail latency; the removed request is deterministic. These warm owner measurements exclude startup, fixture generation, and resource loading.
